clue.text: Form of address becomes part of language

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a form (figure) of address (speech), read word by word
second meaning: a metaphor, simile or similar device used in language

explanation.surface: A way of addressing someone ends up being absorbed into the language.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works piece by piece: form is a figure, and address is a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor or idiom is an expressive device of speech, a figurative turn within ordinary language.

clue.text: Refused to yield — it's very tempting

parts.note: something refused is not allowed
the fruit of labour is its yield

explanation.surface: Someone declined to give way, though the offer was very tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from the apple in Eden, the fruit Adam and Eve were told not to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything desirable precisely because it is prohibited is called this, after the Genesis story of temptation.

parts.note: surface reading: to walk out impolitely
setter's reading: the curt, rude way of telling someone to go away

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as describing a person storming out, but it describes the rude phrase that orders someone else to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a blunt, impolite imperative telling someone to go away.

clue.text: The way to tell someone's driving ability?

parts.note: a road is a way, as in a highway
to sense is to tell or detect

explanation.surface: A question about how to judge whether a person can drive.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the awareness and judgment a motorist or pedestrian shows in traffic, their skill on the highway.

clue.text: He's unpopular when away with the company

parts.note: someone away is out
a theatre company is its cast

explanation.surface: A man is disliked whenever he travels away with his colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah rejected by society is an unpopular person shunned by others.

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of buys
a rabbit is an example of an animal that hops; 'say' signals the example

explanation.surface: A customer purchases the final rabbit in a pet shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A person visiting stores to buy goods is a customer of those stores.

clue.text: Keen ex-head has time to run

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of ex
an age is a period of time
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A keen former headteacher has some time to go running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ex-head' reads as a former principal, but it asks only for the first letter of 'ex'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen means being enthusiastic and impatient to do something, a straightforward synonym.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to get in touch with
second meaning: a noun, a useful person you know

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction, but the verb and the noun phrase are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for getting in touch and a noun for a useful connection in networking.

clue.text: End up well-off by designing flat no one needs

indicators.note: designing is planning out afresh, so the following letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: An architect grows rich by drawing up an apartment nobody actually requires.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to come out of a difficult situation in a good position, like a cat landing safely.

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another comes after it, so the word before 'on' goes second

parts.note: RE is the school-subject abbreviation
a tract is a short published pamphlet

explanation.surface: Pull a pamphlet about religious teaching from circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B, so the publication follows the school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back or withdraw it formally.

clue.text: Stuff revealed by newspaper index, retrospectively

parts.note: a newspaper is an organ, a mouthpiece of opinion

indicators.note: looking back in time means reading the last item from end to start

parts.note: an A-Z is an index, reading A to Z

explanation.surface: Material uncovered by looking back through a newspaper's index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' here is cloth, a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven cloth, and this is a thin, stiff sheer fabric.

indicators.note: interference disrupts a signal, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Pictures distorted by noise disrupting a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a picture, such as a religious painting or a small symbol on a screen.

clue.text: Sign that there is more to come?

definitions.text: Sign that there is more to come?

parts.words: Sign that there is more to come?
parts.note: surface reading: an omen or hint that further events are on the way

parts.words: Sign that there is more to come?
parts.note: setter's reading: a written symbol meaning 'and', showing something else follows

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a portent; it is a typographic character standing for the word 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: The & symbol stands for 'and', which always announces a further item in a list.

parts.note: surface reading: an action likely to cause a furious row
setter's reading: a device whose literal purpose is to set off a blast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive consequences' suggests a scandal or quarrel; it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the device used to trigger a charge, so its job is literally to cause a blast.

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror appears backwards

parts.note: taken as written before reading backwards
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: As mirrored by a shiny metallic material.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a smooth glossy fabric, a kind of cloth woven to shine.

clue.text: Part for actress mixing beer and stout

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actress's role involves blending two kinds of ale in a pub scene.
explanation.definitionFit: In comedy or opera, this is a stock role of a pert, flirtatious maid, played by an actress.

indicators.note: taking something out removes it, here the abbreviation for a unit of time

parts.note: a native is a local resident
T is the abbreviation for time, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A simple-minded local takes a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Being innocent and lacking worldly experience makes someone unworldly and credulous.

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
passé means past it, over and done with

explanation.surface: Someone declares they have got past an obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock where no progress is possible is a figurative obstruction.

clue.text: Agitate pool until it shows sign of contamination

indicators.note: agitating stirs things up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stir the swimming pool until it reveals traces of dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Fouling the environment with harmful substances is contamination, a near synonym.

clue.text: In advance, take care of claim

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: Plan ahead to look after a legal claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend to a title is to lay claim to it, an older sense of the verb.

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone brooded over a terrible setback.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticlimax that fails to meet expectations is a disappointment.

indicators.note: doing something badly means doing it wrongly, so the letters go out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fury erupts when the men perform poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger someone is to provoke or enrage them, which is a verb sense of stirring passion.

parts.note: re means on or about, regarding
the present is now

explanation.surface: A TV programme is currently being broadcast about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun for a programme but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict or portray something is to show it, a verb sense.

parts.note: ex- means former or past
I is the Roman numeral for one
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: Keep going beyond the first road.
explanation.definitionFit: To live on or remain in being is to continue, a near synonym.

indicators.note: setting things out arranges them afresh, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Begin by laying out the points of disagreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaks in a relationship caused by disagreement are differences between people.

parts.note: something in is in fashion
a spire is a part of a church building

explanation.surface: Stir up a trendy part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate a feeling or response in someone is to provoke it.

clue.text: With nothing left, cook ate a broken biscuit

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the remaining letters are rearranged
left here means gone away, so a zero-shaped letter departs from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: With nothing remaining, the cook ate a broken biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: One O is removed from COOK ATE A, and the seven letters left are anagrammed.
explanation.definitionFit: An oatcake is a flat savoury cracker made from oatmeal, a type of Scottish biscuit.

clue.text: Garment gets man's attention, displaying selfish concern

parts.note: a vest is an item of clothing
Ed is a man's name
to show interest is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A man's undershirt draws a lady's eye, revealing his self-regard.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal stake in an outcome, often a financial one, makes someone's involvement self-serving.
